newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Germany's Linde to build Saudi plant.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Linde to build Saudi plant.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's National Industrial Gases Company (GAS) on Sunday said it had awarded German engineering group Linde AG and Riyadh-based Linarco Ltd a contract to build a grassroots air separation plant in Yanbu on the Red Sea.
GAS is 70 percent owned by Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC). The rest is held by a group of Saudi companies.

A company statement on Sunday quoted SABIC's vice-chairman and managing director Ibrahim Ibn Salameh as saying the plant at Yanbu on the Red Sea would produce 1,200 metric tonnes a year of oxygen and 1,500 metric tonnes a year of nitrogen.
He said the total cost of the project was estimated to be around 400 million riyals ($107 million) and was scheduled to be completed in 27 months. The contract was signed on April 7.
"This (the plant) is a very important step for SABIC as well as GAS as the new plant will go a long way in meeting the burgeoning demand for industrial gases," Ibn Salameh said.
GAS was established in 1983. It had doubled its paid-in capital in 1996 to 248 million riyals.
